title: From the Moon to the time on your clock

lessons.objective: Turn a model Earth and follow a place from light into darkness.
Picture a ball beside a lamp to understand the Moon’s changing face.
See how Earth’s little lean changes the sunlight we get.
Follow three clocks to understand why places use different times.

sources.name: NASA Space Place — What causes the seasons?
IANA — Time-zone database and civil-time changes
Royal Museums Greenwich — Local time and the railways

glossary.definition: One of the different views we get of the Moon’s bright side.
An area that follows the same rules for its clocks.

outcomes: Connect day and night to Earth’s rotation.
Explain lunar phases without confusing them with eclipses.
Connect seasons to tilt, sunlight angle and daylight.
Distinguish a time zone from its current UTC offset.
description: Start with day and night, then explore Moon phases, seasons and the clocks we use around the world.
introduction: You do not need a telescope or any astronomy lessons to begin. A ball beside a lamp, the changing evening light and a call to a faraway friend will help us make sense of the sky and our clocks.
prerequisites: No astronomy background needed. The last lesson includes simple clock arithmetic.
